rows: -2500 · Stonehenge's Sarsen Circle Raised — English Heritage dates the sarsen phase to c. 2500 BCE; the ditch and bank are c. 3000 BCE. Sarsen source (West Woods, ~25 km) from Nash et al. 2020.

-2100 · Code of Ur-Nammu Issued in Sumer — Ur-Nammu reigned c. 2112–2095 BCE (middle chronology); some scholars credit the code to his son Shulgi, so the name says 'Code of Ur-Nammu' (its conventional name) rather than 'Ur-Nammu issues'. Renamed from the gap-list wording for that reason.
-1900 · First Palace Built at Knossos — Protopalatial period begins c. 1900 BCE; the visible ruins are mostly from the rebuilt palace. The labyrinth legend is left out (only a suggested connection).
-1473 · Hatshepsut Becomes Pharaoh — The gap list said c. 1479, but that is the start of her regency; she was crowned c. 1473 (Shaw: reign c. 1473–1458). Year moved to 1473 for accuracy.
-1400 · Rigveda Composed — A process over centuries, not one year (some scholars say c. 1700–1100 BCE). Recommend DateFlow-only (manage.py dateflow-only) so it isn't a guessing question.

-1350 · Akhenaten Elevates the Aten Above Egypt's Gods — Renamed from the gap-list 'Introduces the Worship of the Aten': the Aten was worshipped before him; he raised it above all other gods. Whether this was true monotheism is debated.
-1274 · Battle of Kadesh — Year 5 of Ramesses II, c. 1274 BCE in the usual chronology. The Egyptian accounts are royal propaganda; the result was a stalemate.
-1250 · Oracle-Bone Writing Appears in Shang China — Earliest securely dated inscriptions from Wu Ding's reign (c. 1250–1192 BCE); a mature script, so writing may be older. First recognised in 1899.

-1000 · Lapita Voyagers Settle Remote Oceania — A process over two or three centuries (radiocarbon). Recommend DateFlow-only. Countries VU, FJ, TO, WS, PG are new to the countries table (add-country before loading).
-814 · Carthage Founded — 814 BCE is from the Greek historian Timaeus; archaeology supports a foundation in the late 9th century BCE. The Dido story is legend, and the description says so.
-285 · Library of Alexandria Founded — Founding credited to Ptolemy I (advised by Demetrius of Phalerum) or Ptolemy II. Its end was a gradual decline, not one fire: the significance avoids the myth.
40 · Trung Sisters Lead a Revolt Against Han Rule — The revolt ran 40–43 CE.
200 · Teotihuacan's Pyramid of the Sun Built — Construction is usually dated c. 200 CE. The tunnel beneath was long thought to be a natural cave.

239 · Queen Himiko Sends an Envoy to Wei China — Recorded in the Wei zhi section of the Records of the Three Kingdoms. The text gives the second year of Jingchu (238); many historians correct it to 239.
615 · Pakal the Great Becomes Ruler of Palenque — Accession on 29 July 615, from Palenque's inscriptions; died 683.
641 · Arabs Conquer Egypt — The story that Amr burned the Library of Alexandria is a later legend: left out.
825 · Borobudur Completed — Completion usually placed c. 825, in the reign of Samaratungga. Why it was abandoned is uncertain, so the significance doesn't give a reason.
938 · Battle of Bạch Đằng Ends Chinese Rule in Vietnam — Late 938. Ngô Quyền proclaimed himself king in 939.
1050 · Cahokia Grows into a City — Archaeologists call the sudden growth around 1050 Cahokia's 'Big Bang'. Population estimates vary widely.
1100 · Polynesians Settle Hawaii — The settlement date is debated (Kirch; Wilmshurst et al. 2011). Recommend DateFlow-only: a range of over two centuries.
1200 · Lalibela's Rock-Hewn Churches Carved — Tradition credits all eleven to King Lalibela; archaeologists think some may be older or later.

1200 · Polynesians Reach Rapa Nui — Older estimates went as early as 300–800; current radiocarbon work favours c. 1150–1250. The 'ecocide' story is debated, so the significance presents it as debate. Recommend DateFlow-only.
1235 · Sundiata Keita Wins the Battle of Kirina — Known mainly from oral tradition and later Arabic sources; c. 1235 is conventional.
1280 · Polynesian Voyagers Settle New Zealand — Wilmshurst et al. date first settlement to c. 1250–1300.
1293 · Majapahit Founded — Raden Wijaya was crowned in November 1293. The flag connection in the significance is hedged ('often linked').
1325 · Tenochtitlan Founded — 1325 is the date in Mexica tradition, widely used.
1351 · Kingdom of Ayutthaya Founded — Traditional date 4 March 1351, used everywhere.
1352 · Ibn Battuta Visits the Mali Empire — Left Sijilmasa in early 1352; back in Morocco by early 1354.
1438 · Pachacuti Begins the Inca Expansion — 1438 is Rowe's chronology, from Spanish-era sources; radiocarbon work (Marsh et al. 2017) suggests Inca expansion started around 1400.
1450 · Machu Picchu Built — Burger et al. (Antiquity, 2021) date occupation from c. 1420. 'Lost city' is a popular label; local farmers always knew it.
